title: A family member needs help
prompt: A family member needs assistance for several weeks. You want to help, but your work schedule is full.

choices.label: Agree on specific times
choices.text: Offer help twice a week and coordinate with others.
choices.feedback: Clear limits made the commitment more manageable, although it still took time.

choices.label: Take on everything
choices.feedback: You provided a great deal of support. The strain spread into work and recovery time.

choices.label: Help arrange other support
choices.feedback: Paying for support protected time, while reducing your cash buffer.

title: The schedule is wearing you down
prompt: You have been sleeping poorly and missing activities you enjoy. Your next few weeks look just as busy.

choices.label: Protect two evenings
choices.text: Set a boundary and accept a slower pace on optional work.
choices.feedback: Recovery improved several parts of life. You also reduced the time available for optional work.

choices.label: Buy back some time
choices.text: Spend $250 on help with everyday tasks.
choices.feedback: The support eased time pressure, but it became a financial tradeoff.

choices.label: Push through
choices.feedback: You maintained output briefly. The pressure and lost recovery time continued.

title: A community opportunity
prompt: A local organization asks you to help organize an event. There is no pay, and it will use two Saturdays.

choices.label: Lead the event
choices.text: Take responsibility for planning and coordination.
choices.feedback: You practiced leadership and built connections. The opportunity cost was two free Saturdays.

choices.label: Take one small role
choices.text: Volunteer for a shorter, clearly defined task.
choices.feedback: A smaller commitment let you participate while preserving more free time.

choices.label: Decline politely
choices.text: Save the weekends for existing priorities.
choices.feedback: You kept time for other needs and passed on this community experience.

title: An unexpected $500
prompt: You receive a one-time $500 gift. It is not part of your regular income.

choices.label: Keep it available
choices.text: Add the gift to your cash buffer.
choices.feedback: Your cash buffer increased. This is a one-time gain, not a permanent raise.

choices.label: Spend part, save part
choices.text: Save $300 and use $200 for something enjoyable.
choices.feedback: You balanced immediate enjoyment with keeping some of the gift for later.

choices.label: Use it for an experience
choices.text: Spend the whole gift on a meaningful activity.
choices.feedback: The gift funded an experience; your cash position stayed where it was before the gift.

title: A change in the team
prompt: A trusted coworker leaves. You are asked to help a new colleague while everyone adjusts.

choices.label: Create a shared checklist
choices.text: Document routines so more people can provide support.
choices.feedback: The upfront effort created a resource the whole team could reuse.

choices.label: Provide individual support
choices.text: Spend extra time answering questions each day.
choices.feedback: Personal help built trust, while adding demands to your schedule.

choices.label: Focus only on your tasks
choices.text: Wait for the manager to arrange training.
choices.feedback: You protected your own output, but team adjustment took longer.

title: A weekend side project
prompt: Someone offers $650 for a weekend project using your skills. It is outside your regular work hours.

choices.label: Accept the full project
choices.text: Trade a full weekend for the $650 payment.
choices.feedback: The one-time income improved cash. It did not create a permanent pay increase.

choices.label: Negotiate a smaller project
choices.feedback: You earned less and kept more of your weekend.

choices.label: Keep the weekend free
choices.feedback: You gave up the extra income in exchange for time and recovery.
